hints: Focus on what the path of most alpha particles reveals about the volume occupied by matter inside an atom.
If most particles pass through with little deflection, most of the atom cannot contain concentrated matter.
walkthrough: Most alpha particles pass through the foil without significant deflection.
They therefore pass through regions containing very little matter.
Thus most of the atom is empty space, equivalently the nuclear volume is very small compared with the atomic volume.

ai_rubric.observable: States that most of the atom is empty space, or that the nuclear volume is very small compared with the atom.

hints: A very large deflection must result from a strong interaction with a concentrated part of the atom.
Recall the charges of an alpha particle and of the central part of the atom that repels it.
walkthrough: A small number of alpha particles are deflected through angles greater than 90 degrees, so they experience a very strong repulsive interaction.
Because alpha particles are positively charged, the repelling nucleus must be charged positively.
Only a small, concentrated region can produce such rare large deflections, so most of the atom's mass is concentrated in the small nucleus.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the nucleus is charged.
States that the mass is concentrated in the nucleus or in a small central region.

hints: An isotope of P must have P's proton number, even though it may have a different nucleon number.
Use the changes already shown in the sequence: beta decay changes proton number by one but leaves nucleon number unchanged.
walkthrough: P has proton number 84. Since S is an isotope of P, S also has proton number 84.
P decays to Q by alpha emission, so Q has nucleon number 214. The beta-minus decay from Q to R does not change nucleon number, so R also has 214 nucleons.
To reach proton number 84 from R's proton number 83, the next decay is beta-minus; beta-minus decay also leaves nucleon number unchanged.
Therefore S has proton number 84 and nucleon number 214.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the proton number of S is 84.
States that the nucleon number of S is 214.

hints: Q has proton number 82 and R has proton number 83, so the transition is beta-minus decay.
Compare the neutron quark composition udd with the proton quark composition uud.
walkthrough: The increase from proton number 82 in Q to proton number 83 in R shows beta-minus decay, in which a neutron becomes a proton.
A neutron has quark composition udd and a proton has quark composition uud.
Therefore udd changes to uud: one down quark changes to an up quark.

ai_rubric.observable: States that udd changes to uud, or that one down quark changes into an up quark.
